{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — APCN 2 Construction & Maintenance Agreement (Teleglobe USA Inc.)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the APCN 2 consortium agreement — verified findings only

---

## Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, **eight are compliant**, **eight are deviations** requiring redlines, and **two rules have no usable clause** (transition assistance and vendor insurance).

The document is a multilateral consortium construction, ownership and maintenance agreement rather than a vendor supply contract, and several of our standard protections are simply absent. The concentration of risk is in five areas:

1. **No IP indemnity anywhere.** The only indemnity is the reciprocal, share-limited consortium indemnity at 21.2, confined to third-party claims against a Party as an owner of APCN 2; 4.9 and (i)–(iii) expressly disclaim any warranty as to the Supplier or the Wet Segment.
2. **No liability cap at all.** Paragraph 21 makes liability several (21.1) and mutually excludes indirect loss (21.3), but there is no aggregate monetary cap, so our direct liability is unlimited, and there are no uncapped carve-outs.
3. **A 25-year lock-in with penal default consequences.** Paragraph 18 gives us no convenience exit during the Initial Period, Paragraph 7 fixes our Capital Cost and O&M Cost shares for the whole term with no reduction right, and 23.2 permits reclamation of our entire capacity with no payment or credit plus forfeiture of amounts already paid.
4. **No warranty and no governing law.** Subparagraphs 4.9–4.10 disclaim all performance warranties with no pass-through of Supply Contract warranties, and the Agreement designates no governing law, its only forum being a Management Committee that may itself choose the method (potentially foreign-seated arbitration) as the "sole and exclusive remedy".
5. **Housekeeping gaps** on audit controls (9.8/9.9 unlimited, no-notice audits), the Terminal Station Right of Use (11.1 does not reach our Affiliates), transition assistance and insurance.

On the positive side, the assignment regime (Paragraph 22) sits at or above our fallback and is mutual, there is **no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, customer MFN or auto-renewal** burden on us, the MFN-style non-discrimination duties at 15.1–15.2 and 17.1–17.4 run **in our favour**, and the ownership architecture (4.1, 4.3, 12.2, 12.16) vests proportionate ownership and Allocated Capacity in us. We are not disturbing any of these.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | KDD T8 (Para 21.2; 4.9; Para 32) | No IP infringement indemnity anywhere; 21.2 is share-limited and owner-capacity only. Insert fallback-level Subparagraph 21.4 with standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace plus refund, and 3x annual fees super-cap. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | KDD T8 (Para 21.1–21.3) | No aggregate cap and no uncapped carve-outs; fails fallback on two material terms. Add mutual 12-month cost-based cap (Capital Costs and O&M Costs) with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Existing 21.3 exclusion left untouched. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | KDD T8 (4.1, 4.3, 12.2, 12.16, Para 31) | No deliverables, work product or Customer Data provisions; ownership regime runs in our favour and Paragraph 31 restricts rather than licenses our information. Absence of an IP/licence-back architecture noted, not flagged. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subpara 23.1–23.2) | Forfeiture of all amounts paid plus uncompensated reclamation of our capacity is untethered from the default; walk-away territory. Two surgical edits: reclamation must be compensated by payment or credit, and no LD/penalty payable by us. Pre-reclamation accounts remain payable. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | KDD T8 (Para 18.1, 18.2, 18.5) | No convenience exit in the 25-year Initial Period; mid-term exit requires unanimity. Insert Subparagraph 18.8 giving us a 30-day convenience exit with pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. Counterparty side (already better than playbook) untouched; 18.5 and 18.7 unaffected as keyed to 18.1. *(Verification: repaired.)* |
| 6 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | KDD T8 (Para 22.1–22.6; 18.1) | Sits at or above fallback and is mutual; consent not to be unreasonably withheld; no change-of-control trigger anywhere. Consent gate running to the Management Committee, no competitor bar, and undefined "successor"/"Affiliate" noted only. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 (Para 12/Annex 7; p0206, p0208; p0262) | No exclusivity or requirements-purchasing obligation on us; capacity clauses expressly permit IRU sales "without any restrictions". "Sole and exclusive remedy" at p0262 is a forum term reviewed under GOVLAW. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 (Art 21; Paras 12, 15–17) | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant; Paragraphs 15–17 impose duties in our favour. Paragraph 12 capacity-use conditions are mutual structural rules, relaxed at 12.15 and removed at 12.20/12.22. |
| 9 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | KDD T8 (Paras 7.1, 7.2, 18.1, 23.2) | 25-year fixed Schedule B cost shares with no reduction or exit right and penal exit economics — walk-away territory. Insert Subparagraph 7.2A: commitment limited to the current 12-month period, reduction on 30 days' notice, shortfall settled by true-up. Drafted as a Teleglobe-only right. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | KDD T8 (Paras 20, 25, 27.1, 27.2) | No governing law designated; only forum is a Management Committee that may determine the method as the sole and exclusive remedy. Replace with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state and federal courts, retaining the Committee as a resolution step; 27.1 continued-performance sentence and 27.2 untouched. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 4.8–4.10) | All warranties disclaimed with no Supply Contract pass-through — walk-away position. Insert Terminal Party warranty: 90 days conformance for Segment T and software against Annex 8, 30 days for O&M duties, repair/replace/refund. The 4.9 disclaimer protects us via the PG and is not disturbed. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 9.8, 9.9) | Open-ended audit of our books with no notice or frequency limit; F&ASC procedures set no floor. Add once-per-year cap and 15 days' prior notice only. Cost allocation (already better than fallback) and reciprocity untouched. |
| 13 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 11.1; 12.8, 12.14; 22.3(a), 22.6) | Fallback element 2 met via 22.3(a)/22.6; element 1 fails as the 11.1 Right of Use does not reach our Affiliates and 12.8/12.14 are Carrier- and funding-conditioned. Single edit extending 11.1 to Affiliates on written notice. |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | KDD T8 (Paras 18.1–18.7, 31, 32.6; 9.2) | No usable clause: 18.4 is an agreement to agree limited to post-Initial-Period Terminal Party withdrawals; 18.6 distributes sale proceeds, not data. Insert Subparagraph 18.8 at fallback: 90 days' assistance, export within 30 days. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 (Subparas 15.1–15.2, 17.1–17.4; 12.20–12.22) | Non-discrimination duties bind the Terminal Parties (we are not one) and run in our favour; 12.20–12.22 confirm our IRU pricing is a bilateral matter with no obligation to extend best terms. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation on Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 (Art 21) | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant of any kind; Article 21 imposes no hiring restraint. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | KDD T8 (Para 18.1–18.3) | No auto-renewal, notice window or uplift mechanic; continuation past the 25-year Initial Period rests on agreement of the Parties. The one year's notice in 18.1 is our exit right and benefits us. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | KDD T8 (Subpara 5.3; Capital Cost definition, p0133) | Insurance is permissive only and there is no coverage, limit or certificate obligation. Insert Subparagraph 10.10 requiring each Maintenance Authority (counterparty Terminal Parties) to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation cover with certificates on request; 5.3 remains operative. |

---

## Walk-away items

These findings sit in walk-away territory on our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

- **No IP indemnity (INDEMN, Para 21.2/4.9).** No indemnity of any kind covers third-party IP infringement claims arising from what the other Parties provide.
- **Penal default forfeiture (LD, Subpara 23.2).** Loss of our entire capacity with no payment or credit, plus forfeiture of all amounts previously paid, while unpaid accounts remain due.
- **No convenience exit in a 25-year term (T4C, Para 18).** Mid-term termination only by unanimous agreement, with no capital-cost credit on exit under 18.5.
- **25-year take-or-pay cost share with no reduction right (MINCOMMIT, Paras 7.1/7.2/18.1).**
- **Full warranty disclaimer with no pass-through (WARRANTY, Subparas 4.9–4.10).**
- **No governing law and a committee-determined "sole and exclusive remedy" (GOVLAW).** This approaches walk-away territory and should be resolved before signature.

We also note that the **absence of any liability cap (LOL-CAP)** leaves our direct liability unlimited; while assessed as a fallback failure rather than walk-away, we would not recommend signing without it.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations and two missing clauses, comment-tagged `[Playbook]`. New provisions are drafted as inserts (Subparagraphs 21.4, 18.8 for T4C, 18.8 for transition, 7.2A, 10.10) plus surgical edits to 23.2, 9.8/9.9, 11.1 and the dispute-resolution clause, so as to minimise collateral rewrites to a multilateral consortium document.
2. **Reconcile the two proposed Subparagraph 18.8 inserts** (convenience termination and transition assistance) into distinct numbering before the draft goes out.
3. **Escalate the six walk-away items** to the business owner for a signature decision, flagging the 25-year term and the 23.2 forfeiture as the two items with the largest quantum exposure.
4. **Prepare fallback trade positions:** on T4C, expect the counterparty to narrow the pro-rata refund from "any amounts prepaid" to prepaid fees; on WARRANTY, the preferred 12-month software period, compliance-with-laws and malicious-code warranties remain available as a further ask; on LICENSE, contractor coverage and a perpetual paid-up licence were deliberately not pursued.
5. **Confirm signatory entity** — Teleglobe USA Inc. is identified as our signatory at p0322 and is an Initial Party but **not** a Terminal Party; the inserted warranty and insurance obligations are drafted to bind the Terminal Parties/Maintenance Authorities only, and this should be verified against the final execution version.
6. **No action** on the eight compliant rules; the assignment, exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, non-solicit, renewal and IP/ownership positions are acceptable as drafted and, where they exceed our playbook, we will not volunteer changes."}
